note: Thai street food, restaurant dishes, the four regional cuisines and the Thai chains, written for a catalogue that began Malaysian and is becoming Asian. WEB SEARCH WAS UNAVAILABLE FOR THIS ROUND: every figure here is a model estimate reasoned from the dish's own ingredients and anchored against comparable rows already in the catalogue (the pan-Asian round's Thai dishes, the Malaysian noodle and curry rows, the MyFCD component rows). Nothing was read off a published table, so every row is verified:false and source:model_estimate. The ~23 Thai dishes the pan-Asian round already landed — pad thai goong/ayam, pad kee mao, tom yam goong/gai/ikan/campur, tom kha gai, som tam thai, som tam pla ra, larb gai, gai yang, moo ping, khao niao, tod mun pla, khao pad sapparot, kai jeow rice, massaman/green/red curry, yam talay, pandan chicken — are deliberately absent. Portions are the Thai street portion: a one-plate rice dish (khao rad gaeng shape) is a single plate with rice, a noodle bowl is a standard 'lek' bowl, and boat noodles are the small bowl they are actually sold in.
